interest: This document provides valuable insight into the administrative and legal mechanisms governing the liquidation of enemy financial institutions in the United States during World War II, specifically the New York Agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd. It also illuminates the wartime intersection of banking regulation and Latin American diplomacy, illustrating how U.S. authorities and Latin American banks (in Argentina, Brazil, and the Dominican Republic) handled pending drafts, postal transfers, and asset settlements under wartime financial controls.
keywords: Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires
overview: This file consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet (page 2 of decimal file 894.51611) compiled by the U.S. Department of State on a 1943 Government Printing Office form, indexing official correspondence regarding Japanese branch banks in the United States. The recorded entries cover two sub-numbered documents from September 1943 concerning the liquidation and wartime transactions of the Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd. Sub No. 6 details an instruction to the U.S. mission in the Dominican Republic regarding the statutory powers of the New York State Superintendent of Banks in liquidating the bank's New York Agency. Sub No. 5 notes correspondence with C. R. Murray in New York City regarding a message on the payment of a Yokohama draft via postal transfer crediting the account of the Banco do Brasil at the Guaranty Trust Company of New York on behalf of the Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires.

subfiles.summary: This docket sheet indexes State Department correspondence concerning Japanese branch banking operations and liquidations in the United States during World War II. It records Sub No. 6 (dated September 3) to the diplomatic mission in the Dominican Republic concerning the authority of the New York State Superintendent of Banks to liquidate the New York Agency of the Yokohama Specie Bank, Ltd. It also logs Sub No. 5 (dated September 8) to C. R. Murray in New York quoting a communication regarding the settlement of a Yokohama draft via postal transfer to the Banco do Brasil's account at the Guaranty Trust Company.
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Japanese Branch Banks in the United States
